findings.claim: compile_host parses source, linearly searches program.actions, and on non-empty action.inputs serializes the unbounded declared_inputs vector into CompileFailure before calling prepare_scalar_action_host/run_scalar_action (which invokes preflight_source). This bypasses Guard step 0 (validate_config rejecting zero SourceHostBounds before touching source), Guard step 1 (SourceActions, SourceExpressions, SourceStatements, ActionInputs, InputNameBytes, TotalInputNameBytes bounds), and Guard step 3 (crate::validate) on the action-lookup and parameterized-action paths; config.consumer() is also called redundantly in parse_config and compile_host without calling validate_config.

report_sherlock_failure serializes CompileFailure with raw serde_json::to_string and writes directly to stderr via eprintln!("{diagnostic}"), bypassing mori_core::json::export and crate::display::text terminal-control escaping as well as Shell quiet-mode routing. Unlike json::export and core_io::key_export_identity, serde_json::to_string does not escape DEL (\u007f), C1 controls (e.g. \u0085), or Unicode BiDi controls (e.g. \u202e) echoed from untrusted --execution-profile, --action, or source diagnostics.

In commands::compile::run, core_io::read_source(&args.file) executes before checking args.execution_profile.is_some(). When --execution-profile is supplied and FILE is missing, unreadable, or exceeds 1 MiB, the command exits with an ordinary CliError::Read/operation error rather than emitting a structured Sherlock CompileFailure diagnostic on stderr as done for unreadable --execution-config or --target.

CompileFailure omits the status:"failed" tag shown in FIRST-COMPILER-BATCH.md's failed diagnostic shape, and wire::admission includes an extra "bounds" key alongside identity, program_view, and layout (matching AdmissionObservation.bounds); additionally, compile_sherlock labels post-compile serde_json::to_string_pretty(&artifact) errors with stage "observation" even when args.observe is false.
